PullRequest.Title: ci: fix the names of skipped PR checks
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

-->

Skipped checks in the Code OSS workflow show unevaluated expressions and duplicate names, for example on #344148:

- `chat-lib tests (${{ matrix.os }})`
- `Linux (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ strategy.job-total }})`, and the same for macOS and Windows
- `Linux (run)` up to three times, for the Electron-Unit, Electron and Remote jobs

GitHub doesn't evaluate the expressions in a skipped job's name, and doesn't expand the matrix of a job that its `if:` skips. A skipped job that calls a reusable workflow reports under its own name only. This follows up on #344145, which made chat-lib a matrix job, and #342134, which fixed the same problem for the Rust checks.

### Changes

- **chat-lib:** the job is named `chat-lib tests`. GitHub appends the matrix value while it runs (`chat-lib tests (ubuntu-latest)`), and a skipped run shows `chat-lib tests`.
- **Test jobs:** they skip the way the Rust checks already did. The caller always runs (no runner) and passes `affected`. The job inside the reusable workflow skips, and its name is fixed to `Linux`, `macOS` or `Windows`, so each check has one name whether it runs or not (see the table).
- The Linux and macOS workflows drop `job_name`, which only named the job. Windows keeps it for the runner's `JobId` label.
- The tests that pinned the callers' `if:` now check `affected`. A new test fails when a job the changes can skip has an expression in its name.
- The check names in the fix-ci-failures, smoke-tests and integration-tests skills and in the Agent Host E2E README are updated. The README also still described the removed `required-checks` job, so it now refers to PR Gate.

| Job | Before (running) | Before (skipped) | After (both) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Electron unit | `Linux (run) / Electron-Unit` | `Linux (run)` | `Electron-Unit / Linux` |
| Electron integration | `Linux (run) / Electron` | `Linux (run)` | `Electron / Linux` |
| Smoke shards | `Linux (shard 1/2) / Electron-Smoke` | `Linux (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ strategy.job-total }})` | `Electron-Smoke (shard 1/2) / Linux` |
| Browser unit | `Linux (unit) / Browser` | `Linux (unit)` | `Browser-Unit / Linux` |
| Browser integration & smoke | `Linux (integration & smoke) / Browser` | `Linux (integration & smoke)` | `Browser / Linux` |
| Remote | `Linux (run) / Remote` | `Linux (run)` | `Remote / Linux` |
| Agent Host E2E (Windows only) | `Windows (agent host) / Agent-Host-E2E` | `Windows (agent host)` | `Agent-Host-E2E / Windows` |
| Rust CLI | `Linux / CLI` | `Linux / CLI` | `CLI / Linux` |
| Copilot shim | `Linux Copilot Shim / CLI` | `Linux Copilot Shim / CLI` | `Copilot Shim / Linux` |

macOS and Windows follow the same pattern.

### Notes for reviewers

- Branch protection requires only PR Gate, so no required check is renamed (checked with GraphQL `isRequired` on #344148). PR Gate already treats a caller whose inner job is skipped as `skipped`, as it does for `linux-cli-tests` today.
- Smoke tests show one skipped row per shard instead of one per OS, so 3 more rows.
- External dashboards or queries that match the old check names need updating.
- This PR changes `pr.yml` and the test workflows, so every test job should run here and the checks list shows the new running names. The skipped names appear on later PRs that a job can't be affected by, such as docs-only changes.

### How to test

- `cd build && node --test lib/test/detectChanges.test.ts lib/test/agentHostTestSelection.test.ts lib/test/detectMissingCaches.test.ts`: passed (26 tests). Putting back `name: chat-lib tests (${{ matrix.os }})` makes the new test fail, as intended.
- `npm run eslint -- build/lib/test/detectChanges.test.ts build/lib/test/agentHostTestSelection.test.ts`: passed.
- `cd build && npm run typecheck`: passed.
- `actionlint -shellcheck= -pyflakes=` (v1.7.7) on `pr.yml`, `pr-linux-test.yml`, `pr-darwin-test.yml`, `pr-win32-test.yml` and `pr-linux-cli-test.yml`: no new findings compared to `main`. The only findings are the existing unknown-runner-label warnings for the self-hosted pools and `macos-26-xlarge`.
- Pre-commit hygiene hook: passed. None of the changed files are in its scope.

Scenarios.Scenario: PR whose changes affect one or more Linux, macOS, or Windows test groups
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Detect Changes completes, selected reusable workflow jobs allocate runners and execute setup/tests, then PR Gate waits for all selected or skipped job results. The changed caller/inner-job guard placement does not add runner-backed work for selected groups.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Allocate runners, checkout the repository, restore caches, and conditionally download/install dependencies and browsers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per selected logical test job, with two Electron smoke shards per selected platform; unchanged after grouping by job/shard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same reusable workflows, runners, setup, caches, downloads, and test steps ran when the caller-level change-detection condition was true.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations precede tests and therefore remain on the affected-PR critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run compilation and Electron, browser, remote, smoke, Agent Host, Node.js, and Rust test commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same selected suites and shard count as before; no additional subprocess is introduced by the changed guard placement or names.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Affected callers invoked the same reusable workflow and test commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Selected test subprocesses continue to determine job and PR Gate latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The selected test groups and the two smoke shards per platform; effective runner cardinality is unchanged from the base workflow for each affected output.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Selected jobs and smoke shards remain parallel GitHub jobs with the same matrix width. The diff does not add a limiter or increase runner concurrency for affected groups.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing node_modules, built-in-extension, WSL, and test-plan cache behavior is unchanged; cold misses still install/download inside selected jobs, while warm hits bypass those steps.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: every expensive step remains inside the reusable job, and the added `if: ${{ inputs.affected }}` preserves the previous selection condition passed by each caller.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Individual cache-miss and suite durations vary, but the diff does not change their reachability or cardinality when affected.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: affected PRs execute the same runner-backed work with the same concurrency and cache behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Docs-only or otherwise unaffected PR where change detection skips platform test groups
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Detect Changes completes, the now-unconditional caller jobs instantiate reusable workflows, each reusable workflow job immediately skips on `inputs.affected == false`, and PR Gate waits for those skipped results. No runner, checkout, cache, install, or test step is reached.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Instantiate and evaluate a local reusable GitHub Actions workflow, including expansion of two smoke shards per platform.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 22 bounded control-plane entries for an unaffected PR; three more visible rows than before due to smoke matrix expansion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The 19 caller jobs were skipped before reusable-workflow invocation, and the three smoke matrices were not expanded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: PR Gate waits for the skipped results, but no runner-backed boundary is crossed; only GitHub control-plane evaluation is added.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Checkout, cache restore, dependency/browser download, and test execution declared in the reusable workflows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Also zero because the caller itself skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: None; the reusable job-level `if` is evaluated before runner allocation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed workflow inventory: 22 effective platform reusable-workflow entries after matrix expansion (7 Linux, 7 macOS, 8 Windows), rather than 19 skipped caller rows whose three smoke matrices were not expanded.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: GitHub evaluates the reusable workflow entries in parallel. All inner jobs skip before `runs-on`, so effective runner concurrency is zero, as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No caches are read or written because the inner job-level guard prevents runner allocation and all steps; cold versus warm cache state is irrelevant.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that 22 control-plane entries are materialized and zero runners execute, based on caller matrices and the job-level guards in all three reusable workflows.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: GitHub's exact control-plane scheduling latency is external and variable, but the fan-out is small and statically bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: the diff adds only a small bounded control-plane fan-out to stabilize check names, without allocating runners or reaching filesystem, network, or subprocess-heavy steps.

Scenarios.Scenario: Running the build tests that validate change detection and workflow naming
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Node test process synchronously reads and parses workflow YAML while executing the affected test cases; this is test-only and not on VS Code startup, rendering, or product paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read workflow YAML with `readFileSync` and parse it with the YAML loader.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Eight added fixed workflow reads/parses across the changed tests per suite invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The tests loaded only the main PR workflow where needed and did not perform these eight validation reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds a small fixed amount to this build-test suite only; it is off all product critical paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed list of five workflow files plus three reusable workflow reads added to one existing assertion; it does not scale with changed-file count or repository history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reads and YAML parses are synchronous and serial within the test process, as the pre-existing helper already was.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is used; operating-system filesystem caching may make repeated reads warm, but the added count remains fixed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added calls are explicit and synchronous, but their test-only scope and fixed cardinality are also explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact milliseconds depend on filesystem state, but the files and invocation count are small and bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: fixed reads of a handful of small YAML files in a CI unit test do not establish meaningful latency, throughput, CPU, or I/O impact.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete 11-file diff and traced CI orchestration, reusable workflow guards, matrix expansion, PR Gate dependencies, runner-backed setup/test boundaries, caches, and new test-time YAML reads. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not itself fix a demonstrated shipped performance regression.
